html:
The Battle of Okinawa was fought from 1 April to 22 June 1945 on Okinawa, the largest of the Ryukyu Islands, about 550 km south of the main islands of Japan. American forces took the island in the last and bloodiest big battle of the Pacific War.

The United States wanted Okinawa as the base for an invasion of Japan. The Japanese commander, Ushijima Mitsuru, did not defend the beaches. He dug his army into caves and ridges in the south, around Shuri Castle, to make the Americans pay for every hill and to buy time. Offshore, about 1,900 kamikaze suicide planes hit the fleet, sinking about 36 ships and damaging hundreds. On land the fighting went on for 82 days in rain and mud.

About 12,500 Americans and about 100,000 Japanese soldiers died. So did a great many Okinawan civilians, perhaps 100,000, about a quarter of the people of the island; some were pushed into killing themselves by the Japanese army. The cost weighed on American leaders as they planned the invasion of Japan, and was one reason for the atomic bombings in August. The surrender of Japan followed. The United States governed Okinawa until 1972.
